"He himself walked into that school to look for children and actually felt his whole life that he should have died instead of all the boys." Silence After the accident, it was no longer spoken about, says Griffioen. "The children were instructed to keep silent about the disaster. Among themselves they talked a little, of course, but it was not allowed. It had to be hushed up. After the war there was so much suffering that the strategy of mental health care was: silence." Forty years after the disaster, the first commemoration was held. In 2016 that happened for the last time. Until now. "At first I thought: I don't want this anymore," says Dies Griffioen. "But then that whole fear from the past creeps back. Like at our home, that the accident was not processed. That means you continuously have a kind of gigantic grief," she explains. "And that is as if a thin film is removed from the wound. And then it all comes back up." Griffioen today reflects on the boys who died, but also on the great grief of the surviving relatives. "It is also a kind of commemorating and acknowledging the grief."

title: Several cars set on fire in Zoetermeer parking garage, witnesses sought
lead: In a parking garage in Zoetermeer, several cars have been set on fire in recent times. The first fire was on 14 August and last week fires followed on 30 September and 4 October. In the night from Monday to Tuesday, two cars were set on fire and an attempt was made to set a third on fire, reports the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Cars parked next to the burning cars also sustained damage. All fires were at night. The police are investigating whether there is a connection between the arsons and call on witnesses to come forward. Camera surveillance Above the parking garage on the Parkdreef are homes. During the last fire of last night, residents had to leave their homes for some time. The municipality of Zoetermeer is installing camera surveillance, reports the Zoetermeers Dagblad . The hope is that this prevents new incidents. In addition, thanks to the surveillance, intervention can happen sooner.

title: Hoogeveen has had enough after days of unrest: 'They want to fight with police'
lead: In the quiet centre of Hoogeveen this afternoon, a terrace visitor points curiously at a group of teenagers hanging around near a monument. "Are those the children sitting there?", he asks a restaurant employee. "Yes", the employee explains. "But they can go far, you know." During the day, the Kerkplein near the Hoofdstraat is still peaceful, but in recent evenings fireworks, eggs and stones flew through the air. Passers-by and entrepreneurs are being intimidated by a group of young people between 10 and 17 years old. That is why the municipality of Hoogeveen is intervening. Mayor <entity id="person:martijn-breukelman">Martijn Breukelman</entity> is designating a safety risk area with effect from today after evenings of unrest, in order to be able to carry out preventive searches. The cameras that were installed a few days ago had not yet had the desired effect. Nor had the ban on assembly. The municipality is not entirely clear about where the unrest comes from. Boredom may play a role. "But it concerns behaviour that we absolutely do not accept", mayor Breukelman emphasises. That is why the municipality has had enough: "The time for consultation is over, we are now taking firm action." Unsafe For entrepreneurs and residents, the situation has become untenable. Erwin Slomp, chairman of Stichting Binnenstad Hoogeveen, sees how the retail climate is suffering from the unrest. "People no longer feel safe when cobras or other fireworks are thrown at them. Shopkeepers and their staff are being intimidated and visitors no longer dare to enter the Hoofdstraat. This is a line that has been crossed." In recent evenings, several young people were pulled off their fatbikes by police, detained or fined. During searches, police found not only fireworks, but also knives and knuckledusters. Almost all of them are minors, so police will also talk to the parents. 'Dead village' According to the youths in the centre this afternoon, the rioters' motive is mainly a combination of boredom, group pressure and a craving for sensation. "People just want to act tough and show that they are mafia," says a 15-year-old boy on a fatbike. "They just want to fight with the police." A blond boy of just 13 years old says that the boys causing nuisance in the evenings know each other from Hoogeveen. They come from different schools. In online groups they urge each other to come too. "Finally something is happening in this dead village. When everyone is there, it is fun. Now it is mainly provoking the police with fireworks and then driving away as fast as possible." He does understand that the situation is getting out of hand: "My parents find it awful. I am still allowed to meet up in the evening but actually not to come to the centre anymore." A question about whether he will listen to his parents is answered only with a smile. Call to parents Together with the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, the municipality is mapping the identity of the troublemakers. More than 65 names are already known. Their parents can all expect a letter. Both the mayor and the city centre association explicitly point to the role of the guardians. Breukelman: "14- or 15-year-olds with knives or knuckledusters, that is no longer mischief." And Slomp also makes an urgent appeal to parents: "Know where your child hangs out in the evening and what it does. There is also a responsibility of your own there."

title: Suspect in Herkenbosch murder now also suspected of murdering his own mother
lead: Daniel B., the German man suspected of the murder of Paul Vossen from Herkenbosch in Limburg, is now also suspected of murdering his mother. The justice authorities announced this this afternoon in the court in <entity id="org:gemeente-roermond">Roermond</entity>. The woman has been missing for almost two years. Police and justice authorities already had "strong indications" that B. had something to do with his mother's disappearance, but not enough for a formal suspicion of murder. Now that is therefore different. The Public Prosecution Service has not disclosed what new evidence or leads there are. The 48-year-old B. was questioned last month about his mother's disappearance. In a storage space in the German municipality of Heinsberg, items with the woman's blood were previously found. In another storage space, which was in her name, there were shovels and a rake. The woman had no garden of her own. The police suspect that the items were used to bury the woman. B. denies all involvement in her disappearance. He also says he has nothing to do with the death of Paul Vossen. Home robbery Daniel B. was arrested in September last year on suspicion of the murder of Vossen, earlier that month. The OM thinks that the man was killed during a failed home robbery. Vossen (66) had just retired and was found with severe injuries in the garden of his villa in Herkenbosch. He died shortly afterwards. B. lived not far from Herkenbosch at that time. The apartment in Montfort where he was arrested was in the name of his mother Teresa Krug. The woman of Polish origin had not been seen since March 2025, but was never reported missing. Searches for her body have so far yielded nothing. The two cases are being handled simultaneously, writes L1 Nieuws . That will probably happen next year.

title: Ten injured in stabbing at school in Poland, suspect (19) arrested
lead: Ten people were injured in a stabbing at a school for vocational education in the north of Poland. A 19-year-old student of the school could be arrested in the vicinity. The injured are five students, two teachers, two bystanders and the perpetrator. The latter injured himself, local authorities report. No one is in life-threatening danger. One person did sustain serious injuries and a number of victims were taken to a hospital by helicopter. The attack with a "sharp object" took place around 11:00 in Ostroleka, about 120 kilometers northeast of Warsaw. The authorities have not disclosed anything about a possible motive. The police shared a photo of the arrest: The suspect could be detained less than a kilometer from the school, after he had fled. He was taken to the hospital with unknown injuries. Two hours after the attack, the mayor of Ostroleka announced that the school will remain closed, so that the authorities can investigate the site of the attack.

title: Extensive mortgage fraud by criminals, report has been lying in a drawer for months
lead: In recent years, between 6,000 and 11,000 homes in the Netherlands have been bought with forged papers. By committing fraud when applying for the mortgage, criminals manage to get the homes into their hands in order to carry out illegal activities there. That is stated in a not yet published report that, according to insiders, has been lying at the Ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> for more than six months. The report was drawn up by the Financial Expertise Centre, which was given the assignment by the previous <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity> to conduct research into the "nature and extent" of mortgage fraud in the Netherlands. Members of parliament, but also the Dutch Association of Banks (NVB) and the professional association of <entity id="org:zbo-notarissen">notarissen</entity>, have been very concerned about this form of fraud for some years. Criminals manage to buy properties with the help of, for example, forged payslips, employer statements, annual figures or tax returns. Undermining The purchased homes are used for "money laundering, illegal rental, labour exploitation, drug crime and other forms of undermining", said NVB chair Medy van der Laan today in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. She was there for a hearing on undermining crime. The results of the report, which was supposed to be ready in March, have been awaited for months. "Mortgage fraud is increasingly taking place," said Van der Laan. "Exploitation is taking place, deception and other very terrible things. And it disrupts the livability of a neighbourhood." In 2024, reports already emerged via Het Financieele Dagblad about a criminal network that bought hundreds of homes in the Amsterdam region between 2018 and 2023 through manipulation. Those properties turned out to have been used for, among other things, storage of money and drugs, and labour migrants were housed there. The fraudsters, mostly Bulgarian labour migrants, had been hired by administrative offices to forge payslips. In the Tweede Kamer, among others, VVD and NSC asked questions about it to the then cabinet. Pro has also long been urging measures. The Royal Dutch Association of Civil-law Notaries (KNB) also points to "flawed legislation" and "limited possibilities for information exchange". Checking with the tax authority Just like banks, notaries would like the possibility to verify income data with the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>. That should not be a problem. "We respect all sensitivities around privacy. For an application, we only want to check whether the data we have received are correct," said Van der Laan. MP Mutluer of Pro is urging that the report and the recommendations now be sent to the Kamer as quickly as possible. Next week, a debate on this subject is also scheduled.

title: 200,000 Yemenis flee due to reignited fighting
lead: The UN organization for migration and aid to refugees (IOM) is raising the alarm about the situation in Yemen. Since the reignition of the battle between the Houthis and the government army, at the beginning of last month, around 200,000 Yemenis have fled. "People are running for their lives but find safety nowhere," says IOM director Amy Pope. "They now need shelter, food and safety. Our people are on the ground, but the funding is not." Pope is asking donor countries to take action. "Yemen must not become a forgotten crisis. The world has the means to help. They must be used now." Nearly thirteen years For many refugees, it is not the first time they have had to leave their place of residence. The civil war in Yemen has already lasted more than thirteen years. It began with an uprising by the Iran-backed Houthis. The government army has the support of Saudi Arabia. Through UN mediation, a ceasefire was reached in 2022. That was broken last month by an offensive by the Houthis. They gained control of the entire area along the Red Sea. From there, airports, military complexes and oil installations in Saudi Arabia are being fired upon with rockets and drones, again today as well. The conquests increase the Houthis' ability to fire on shipping traffic in the Strait of Bab al-Mandab, the connection between the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government army have begun a counteroffensive to push back the Houthis. The fighting is currently taking place mainly near the town of Dhubab on the Red Sea and in the area south of the city of Ta'izz. These are images from Monday of the government army's offensive near the Strait of Bab el-Mandeb:

title: House of Representatives in favour of alcohol meter for convicted persons
lead: A majority of the House of Representatives supports the introduction of the alcohol meter. That is an ankle bracelet for people who have been convicted of a crime in which alcohol played a role, and who have been given an alcohol ban by the court. It can involve, for example, a traffic accident or domestic violence. The alcohol meter absorbs skin moisture and sweat and detects whether alcohol is present in it. The probation service receives a notification upon alcohol intake and contacts this person. If it has been established that the person has indeed been drinking, and that it was for example not cleaning agent that someone was working with, then a warning follows. Pilots The law has already been prepared by previous cabinets but is only now before the House. The alcohol meter was tested in pilots in which convicted persons could voluntarily choose the ankle bracelet instead of urine and blood tests. In 2023, nearly 1500 people were given an alcohol ban or an alcohol and drugs ban. Of the people with an alcohol meter, 10 percent committed an offence while wearing the ankle bracelet, compared to 51 percent of the persons with only urine checks. These more positive effects were also present three months after disconnecting the ankle bracelet, according to police figures. Not refusing A refusal to wear the alcohol meter while the court has prescribed an alcohol ban is regarded as refusing a punishment. This also applies to attempts to remove the ankle bracelet. Alcohol meters cost around 1500 euros. In case of destruction or loss, the wearer must pay the costs. Unlike an ankle bracelet, an alcohol meter cannot track where someone is.

title: 'Drifting' motorcyclist gets community service for fatal accident in Lelystad
lead: A motorcyclist who caused a fatal accident in Lelystad two years ago has been sentenced to 240 hours of community service. The 32-year-old man must also pay 37,000 euros in damages to the victim's parents. The accident happened on 2 June 2024 on the Karperweg in Lelystad during an illegal 'drift' event. Hundreds of spectators were present. When drifting on a motorcycle, the rider deliberately loses grip on the rear wheel and the rear wheel slides sideways through the bend. The motorcyclist from Schiedam ended up on the wrong side of the road and collided head-on with a cross motorcycle. The 18-year-old rider of that motorcycle from Maarssen died two days later from his injuries, writes Omroep Flevoland . Motorcycles gone The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded eight months in prison. The court arrives at a much lower sentence, partly because the man from Schiedam had no criminal record and has expressed regret. After the fatal accident, the man got rid of his motorcycles and says he never wants to ride a motorcycle again. According to the judge, the man was careless and inattentive, but not reckless. The court writes in the verdict that the suspect, although fatal, in fact violated one traffic rule: not keeping sufficiently to the right. According to the OM, there was an illegal street race, but the judge does not agree. Participants did drift, but according to the court it was not about speed. A 36-year-old man from Rotterdam who according to the OM was the organizer of the drift event has been acquitted of manslaughter. According to the court, he did not organize an illegal street race and it cannot be established with certainty whether he gave the starting signal for the drift with the fatal outcome.

title: Couple in US charged with abuse in 'horror house' full of surrogate children
lead: A couple from California has been charged in a case involving the abuse of at least fifteen children between the ages of two months and thirteen years. Fourteen of the children are said to have been born via surrogacy. According to prosecutors, the children were beaten and punched by nannies in the couple's villa. Guojun Xuan (66) and Silvia Zhang (39) kept most of the children in their villa in Arcadia, about 20 kilometers from Los Angeles. The children were taken in at their home and cared for by nannies, prosecutors stated. They are said to have spent hours a day in three different rooms of the villa, so-called 'learning centers', where the nannies supervised. Last year, 32 surveillance cameras were found in the villa. According to the prosecution, the couple used them to keep an eye on the nannies. Footage recorded how they systematically beat and harshly punished the children. The couple is accused of having recruited women to become surrogates and of having conspired to have the children abused. Prosecutor Nathan Hochman called the villa a "horror house". "The number of children exposed to this alleged horrific abuse is unprecedented," he said. The couple was arrested yesterday and says it is innocent. According to American media, they wanted to create a large family. Head injury The investigation started after a two-month-old baby with head injuries was brought into the hospital, in July last year . One of the nannies is said to have hit the newborn baby on the head. Hospital staff did not trust it and notified the police. An arrest warrant was already issued for the nanny last year, but she is said to still be on the run. 21 children who were under the couple's supervision were placed elsewhere: fifteen were removed from the villa and six were elsewhere. Most of the children were between one and three years old. The couple was already detained at the time, because they are said to have known that their baby was injured and did not raise the alarm. The couple was released on bail because no formal charge had yet been filed. Now that the Public Prosecution Service and the police have completed the investigation, the two could be arrested again. Surrogates In addition to the abuse, the couple is also suspected of making false statements to at least two women who became surrogates. Zhang is said to have said that she had difficulty getting pregnant. Prosecutors expect that the surrogates came from different parts of the United States and that they did not know that others were also carrying embryos for the two.

title: Police in Bavaria searching for a puma or something that looks like one
lead: A municipality close to Munich Airport in the German state of Bavaria is calling on residents to be careful because a wild feline animal has been sighted. It may be a puma. The police have launched a large search operation. A helicopter and drones have been deployed. The animal was spotted last night by a hunter with night-vision equipment. That was in the Notzinger Moos nature reserve, a few kilometres from the airport. He made a video of it. The images were viewed by experts last night and they concluded that it may be a puma. No panic The municipality of Erding, which sent the warning out into the world, does not want to cause panic. "We want to make sure that people keep a slightly better eye on their surroundings," a spokesperson told regional broadcaster BR . Anyone who sees the animal or knows where it is staying should not go towards it but call the police immediately. Dog owners are advised to keep their dog on a leash. "And do not let your small children play outside unsupervised," the spokesperson said. Puma and lion It would not be the first time that an animal in Germany was mistaken for a puma or lion. Last year, a search operation for a puma was also launched in the state of Saxony-Anhalt. It was not found. According to an expert, it must have been a cat. In 2023, police in Berlin spent 30 hours searching for a lion that was said to have escaped. That one was not found either. It was presumably a wild boar.

title: Nieuw-Lekkerland defaced in many places with swastika in flag of Israel
lead: In Nieuw-Lekkerland in the <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">provincie Zuid-Holland</entity>, defacements with swastikas have been found in dozens of places. The municipality is filing a report. Het Reformatorisch Dagblad reported earlier about the defacements. In images shared by the newspaper, paving stones can be seen on which Israeli flags have been sprayed with a paint spray can. In the places where the Star of David should be, there is a swastika. The graffiti is being removed. Possibly a number of tiles will have to be replaced. Mayor <entity id="person:theo-segers">Theo Segers</entity> of the <entity id="org:gemeente-molenlanden">gemeente Molenlanden</entity>, under which Nieuw-Lekkerland falls, calls the defacements to news agency ANP "very reprehensible". Not the first time According to the municipality, the swastikas were applied last night. A spokesperson reports that defacements have now been removed at approximately thirty locations. "Possibly they will be found in even more places." The municipality expects everything to be cleaned up tomorrow. It is not the first time that swastikas have been applied in the public space of Nieuw-Lekkerland. That also happened earlier this year. At that time, street furniture and bus shelters were defaced because of the possible arrival of an asylum seekers' centre. A resident of the place then decided to stick stickers with hearts on the swastikas : It is exactly three years ago today that the terrorist organisation Hamas carried out a major attack on Israel. More than 1200 people were killed and 251 people were taken hostage. Today, the attacks by Hamas are commemorated in many places around the world, including in the Netherlands, among others in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>.

title: Mayor of Oldebroek at Coming Out Day celebration after council scrapping lgbti policy
lead: Oldebroek hoists the rainbow flag on Coming Out Day, but not at the town hall. The Christian-conservative council of the Veluwe municipality decided last week officially to stop lgbti policy and no longer hoist the rainbow flag. That was already in the coalition agreement of the Christelijk Verbond Oldebroek (CVO), the SGP and Algemeen Belang Oldebroek (ABO). At the Kruiskerk the rainbow flag will indeed flutter on Saturday. And mayor <entity id="person:tanja-haseloop-amsing">Tanja Haseloop-Amsing</entity> will be present when the flag is hoisted, although the council decided to continue "without woke expressions". Haseloop-Amsing (VVD) says to Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> that she is not only chair of the college of mayor and aldermen, but that she has her own role and her own line. "As mayor I am also an independent administrative body, which must keep an eye on the fact that in this village we also still treat each other reasonably well. That there is administrative integrity. That role as mother of the municipality I now take on." Flag action Reverend Han Wilmink of the Kruiskerk will hoist the flag, just like every year. He thinks it is extra important this year. "This municipal policy gives people a sign: you do not belong. We must oppose and resist that." State secretary <entity id="person:claudia-van-bruggen">Claudia van Bruggen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity>, who comes from the region, will also be there, Trouw writes. After the presentation of the coalition agreement in July, resident Kjeld Mooi decided to stand up against the plans of the municipal government to scrap the lgbti policy. At the installation of the council he stood with a rainbow flag in front of the town hall. He received much support for his action, including from lgbti people in the municipality who said that they always have to hide their orientation. Coming Out Day is on Sunday 11 October, but the organisation in Oldebroek is already holding the meeting on Saturday, out of respect for the Sunday rest. Everyone in the village who wants one can get a rainbow flag to hang out at home on Saturday. More than 250 flags have already been requested.

title: Temporary protection or asylum? Ukrainians do not really know where they stand
lead: Mixed feelings among Ukrainians after it became known that their asylum applications must be reviewed. "On the one hand there is slight hope that an end will come to the temporary nature of our stay, on the other hand we still do not know where we stand," says Ukrainian Jamal Statsenko. An experience that Anna Bieliaieva of Vital'nya, a community for Ukrainian refugees in the Netherlands, shares. "We increasingly hear that people are aware of the European ruling, but what will happen now remains unclear." The European Court of Justice ruled last week that the Netherlands must get to work on assessing the asylum applications of more than 140,000 Ukrainians. A problem for <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, because the asylum system will thus come under even more pressure. 'Do we have to go back, or are we staying here?' For the Ukrainians who fled their country after the outbreak of the war, the Temporary Protection Directive was activated for the first time. A European rule devised to quickly offer temporary protection in a situation of a large influx of refugees. As a result, Ukrainians immediately received the right to shelter, work, medical care and education for the children. "Since the beginning of the war they have actually been in a very pleasant waiting room. But even if you are in a waiting room that is very comfortable, it remains a waiting room," says Mark Klaassen, assistant professor of immigration law at <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity> University. From Europe, the protection is extended time and again, by now until March 2028. But it remains the question what will happen after that. According to Ukrainians, that uncertainty is the big problem. "My son has lived half his life here. He speaks Dutch, has his social life with friends here," says Bieliaieva. "Lately he keeps asking which school he will go to after group 8. Do we have to go back, or are we still here? I cannot give an answer to that." Tidal wave of asylum applications The advantage of that special European rule is that an individual asylum procedure does not have to be completed. As a result, immigration services do not suddenly have to process an enormous number of applications. That is where the Netherlands went wrong. The rule has been worked out here in such a way that Ukrainians had to submit an asylum application, after which they received that temporary European protection. The asylum applications were then paused until the temporary protection expires. That is not allowed, the European Court now says: the asylum applications are separate from the temporary protection. Since the Netherlands had the Ukrainians submit such an application, those must also be reviewed. A headache file for the ministry. "Let alone for the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity>, which currently has to deal with a backlog of more than 50,000 people waiting for a decision. On top of that, they see this tidal wave of assessments coming at them," says Klaassen. Ukrainians are now not building up a right of residence. "With an asylum status you build up years of residence, after five years you could in theory become Dutch. Those years do not count for Ukrainians now," says the assistant professor of immigration law. Uncertainty remains It will still take a while before Ukrainians hear anything about their asylum application. Asylum minister Van den Brink wants to first process the people who are arriving now, then work through the waiting list and after that the group of Ukrainians will have their turn. He does emphasise in a letter to the House today that the European ruling has no effect on the way in which the reception of Ukrainians by municipalities is currently organised. According to Statsenko, an asylum status would help him get his own home. "With temporary protection, the chance that you get a mortgage is very small. It is also much harder to rent; landlords make difficulties about that temporariness." It is not the case that all Ukrainians are waiting for such an asylum procedure, says Bieliaieva. "Of course there are people who would like to go back. We love Ukraine and of course we would preferably never have left." Until the ministry has worked out how it will concretely tackle this situation, it remains a waiting game. "I hope to finally get clarity for the future and not another temporary extension," says Statsenko. Bieliaieva also wants to get the opportunity to really build something here. "It would be nice if we know where we stand. But at its core not much changes. What this exactly means, we do not know."

title: Pro-Palestinian protest with expressions of support for Hamas in Amsterdam disbanded
lead: A pro-Palestinian protest on Dam Square in Amsterdam has been disbanded by <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity>. At the demonstration, slogans were chanted such as 'long live the 7th of October', referring to Hamas's attacks in Israel on 7 October 2023. Demonstrators also burned an Israeli flag. Protesters with face masks held up a large green banner on which the slogan 'we support Hamas' can be read. Men with scarves over their faces held a banner that said 'glory to our martyrs, victory to the resistance'. Not breaking the law The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> looked at the expressions on Dam Square and judged that the texts on the banners do not break the law. Asked whether such texts are not tasteless on the day that the massacre Hamas carried out in Israel three years ago is commemorated, one organiser responds: "Tasteless? I don't know. It is provocative and I do understand why people do it." The man is angry because of a law being drafted to make glorification of terrorism a criminal offence. According to the man, the Netherlands should not see Hamas as a terrorist organisation but as a political movement, and support for it should not become punishable. Demonstrators who walked on from Dam Square into the city wanted to go to the neighbourhood where many Jewish buildings are located. The police prevented the group from going that way, after which the group continued protesting in front of the door of the Stopera, the city hall. There an Israeli flag was set on fire. An estimated 150 demonstrators were present on Dam Square, about half of them then walked on into the city. At 20:15 the demonstration was disbanded on the orders of the mayor, because part of the demonstrators did not follow the instruction to go to the Stopera. "This created a fear of disorder", says a municipal spokesperson. The protesters then left the area.

title: Six arrests for theft of Renoir paintings in the south of France
lead: A month after the painting theft from the Renoir museum in the south of France, the French police have arrested six suspects. Among them are the two suspected burglars, French media report. The arrests were made in four different departments in the south and east of France. The six are suspected of, among other things, theft in an organised context. They have been transferred to Nice for questioning. On 8 September, four paintings by the famous French impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir were stolen from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mers. The two thieves left two paintings behind in the museum's garden during their escape. Most valuable paintings It is not yet clear whether the other two have already been found. It concerns the works Madame Colonna Romano and Jeune Femme au puits (Young woman at the well). The paintings were on loan from Musée d'Orsay in Paris. The thieves seemed well prepared. They entered around 06.00 in the morning via a glass door and took the canvases in less than 3 minutes. They were the four most valuable pieces of the museum. It was opened in 1960 in Renoir's last residence. When the police arrived there, it turned out that part of the fencing had been cut through, allowing the perpetrators to enter the grounds. Security footage later showed that the thieves had sawn through the anchoring of the paintings in the wall.

title: Face of Spanish housing protests Maricarmen Abascal (87) has died
lead: Maricarmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman who became the face and namesake of the housing protests in Spain, has died. That has been announced by the Spanish tenants' union. Abascal was evicted from her house, where she had lived for seventy years. Due to a rent increase she could no longer afford her house. Her eviction was the direct cause of the protests in Spain. Many Spaniards cannot afford housing due to inflation and a shortage of housing. Especially in the cities Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia there is too little housing. The country also has a large shortage of social housing. It concerns less than 2 percent of the available supply, while the European average is 8 percent. Maricarmen quickly became the face of the housing crisis in Spain: At Abascal's eviction hundreds of demonstrators were present. They regarded it as a new low point in the country's housing crisis. The activists tried to stop the clearance, but the police dispersed them with tear gas. In the end the eviction was reversed and the woman could continue living in her house. Decrees adopted Yesterday the Spanish government approved two housing market decrees. The measures for rent caps, a temporary ban on evictions and restrictions on the purchase of homes by companies were, according to Prime Minister Sánchez, "based on pure common sense". He stated that opinion polls showed that a large majority of the population is in favour of intervention in the housing market. The same decrees were rejected by parliament last week. Sánchez then called early elections for 29 November. Due to the dissolution of parliament, the measures can now be introduced temporarily and subsequently submitted to a smaller permanent body of 69 parliamentarians that remains in place during the election period. There is sufficient support there to keep the measures in place. The decrees have also been named after Maricarmen Abascal. Prime Minister Sánchez has expressed his condolences to the surviving relatives after her death.

title: Climate change cause of rapid decline of chinstrap penguins on British island
lead: British scientists have established that the population of chinstrap penguins on a British island in the Southern Ocean has declined dramatically. In 2011, 900,000 chinstrap penguins and 90,000 macaroni penguins lived on Zavodovski Island. Fourteen years later, the number of chinstrap penguins had fallen by 63 percent, while the number of macaroni penguins had actually increased. The scientists of the British Antarctic Survey (BAS) explain the "alarming" decline of the first group by climate change. The diet of chinstrap penguins consists mainly of krill: small shrimp-like creatures. "Because the water warmed, the krill disappeared to the south," BAS scientist Norman Ratcliffe says to the BBC . "Due to the sea ice in the south and the absence of suitable islands to nest, the chinstraps cannot follow their food." The fact that the macaroni penguins are doing well is presumably because they have a more varied diet; those animals also eat fish and shellfish. Other explanations The researchers also looked at other possible explanations for the decline of the chinstrap penguin, such as the volcanic eruption on Zavodovski Island in 2016 and the competition from other hunters of krill, such as the macaroni penguins, whales and the fishing industry. These alternative explanations turned out not to be tenable. The chinstrap penguins also occur on other islands in the Antarctic region. There too, scientists see the numbers declining. The BAS scientists think that the chinstrap penguins will end up on the list of endangered species if the trend continues. Their research can be found in Current Biology .

title: Discontent in Japan grows after arrest of American serviceman for murder of woman

Fear, sadness, anger, mourning, shame and also desire and ambition, what the ancient Greeks call pathos. We joke pain away or declare fear and anger outside the prevailing order. Good hope among local administrators after Jetten's speech
lead: Local administrators react positively to the words that Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> spoke on Tuesday about cooperation and covering the costs for youth care by the national government.

title: 'I saw with my own eyes how he stabbed him without stopping.' What happened on board the FlyDubai flight in eight videos
lead: On Wednesday 30 September, flight FZ 1073 was hijacked by a pilot with Omani nationality. NRC selected eight videos showing what happened on board the plane.

title: Sylvana Simons and Bob Scholte would have done better to talk to each other at the kitchen table
lead: Thomas Hogeling weekly considers public opinion. What is said and especially what is not said? This week: polemic on the left.

title: Oscar winner Eva Marie Saint (102) died
lead: The American actress Eva Marie Saint has died. The Oscar-winning actress, who among other things played in the film North by Northwest, was 102 years old. She died a natural death, a spokesperson for the family says.

title: Overijssel: a deal is a deal on the arrival of the Nedersaksenlijn
lead: The province of Overijssel has called on minister <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Vincent Karremans</entity> to honour the agreements that were made about the Nedersaksenlijn. 'A deal is a deal', says provincial executive member Martijn Dadema. 'We have raised all kinds of expectations among residents. It affects the relationship between citizens and government if you fail to honour such important agreements.'

title: Climate crisis destroys one of Europe's icons: no more snow on the Matterhorn
lead: The problem of melting glaciers is not limited to Switzerland, regardless of what climate deniers with a BBB level of thinking claim about it

title: Return hubs for rejected asylum seekers: 'A total black box'
lead: Five European countries, including the Netherlands, are working on an initiative to send rejected asylum seekers to a country outside the European Union. Those reception locations are also called return hubs. The Greek asylum minister said this week that the project will start in early 2027. The first refugees may go to Rwanda. But we are then also distancing ourselves from all human rights. "As soon as you outsource that responsibility, it is completely completely out of our hands," says Member of the European Parliament for Volt Anna Strolenberg in De Rode Draad. She has just returned from the area and tells what she saw there.

title: Bizarre Africa Cup soap gets sequel at the CAS: will the title stay in Moroccan hands?
lead: It was one of the craziest finals ever. Senegal walked off the pitch in anger after a penalty was awarded to Morocco in stoppage time. It was missed, after which Senegal still won the Africa Cup in extra time. The title was later taken away on regulatory grounds by the African football association, after which Senegal went to the CAS, which will consider the case on Thursday.

title: Ozempic with an o
lead: The brand name of the drug is evolving into a generic name, FD columnist Anna Dijkman observes. The common parlance will not be reined in.

title: Shia LaBeouf and Mia Goth are divorcing: 'Irreconcilable differences'
lead: Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf. The 32-year-old actress cites "irreconcilable differences" as the reason for the break, American media such as Page Six and TMZ report. Earlier this year it already came out that the two are no longer together.

title: Shell and ExxonMobil plunder NAM coffers from which compensation for earthquake damage victims must come
lead: The Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM) is paying a dividend of 1.4 billion euros to Shell and ExxonMobil

title: A pure chemical mirror image leads to philosophical life questions. And to a Nobel Prize
lead: Important molecules for life, such as amino acids and proteins, are all left-handed. How is that possible? Because a molecule can also have a mirror image. For pharmaceutical companies that can be useful.

title: Never happened before: Paulien Cornelisse sets posthumous record with 7 books at once in bestseller list
lead: Paulien Cornelisse has set a record in the weekly bestseller list a week after her death. This week, seven books by the writer, who died as a result of cancer, are back in the Bestseller 60. According to books umbrella organisation CPNB, this has never happened before in the history of the list.

title: Reform of box 3 need not be a problem for the treasury
lead: The small saver remains out of the firing line in the reform of box 3. But who pays then? The bill can be placed elsewhere, argue Flip de Kam and Jan Donders.

title: Residents of Rome completely fed up with tourists in golf carts
lead: In Rome they are being spotted increasingly often: tourists who have themselves driven in golf carts past all the sights. Many residents would rather see the little carts go than come. "The city is turning into a real transport jungle."

title: Kabinet wil telefoons vanaf januari uit scholen

title: Evenepoel takes European cycling title in Slovenia
lead: Remco Evenepoel won the European cycling title in Slovenia on Sunday. The Belgian beat the Italian Giulio Ciccone in an exciting sprint à deux. Another Italian, Christian Scaroni, finished third at just under a minute.

title: Safe haven for self-employed? Entrepreneurs question new Self-Employed Act
lead: The bill that must make clear whether you can work as a self-employed person still raises many questions among entrepreneurs themselves. They are happy with the 'legal recognition'. But the many criteria cause clarity. "The unrest that this law precisely wants to solve remains."

title: Dutch streaming services increasingly better watched
lead: Among the American streaming services, providers such as NPO Start and Videoland are attracting a growing number of viewers.

title: Churches call on ING to stop with fossil fuels; should the church make such a political statement?
lead: Churches will ask ING in a letter to stop investing in fossil fuels. This is on the initiative of the Micha Nederland foundation. Director Harmen Niemeijer-Scheffer does not think he is being political. "This is simply putting a question," he says on Dit is de Dag.

title: A bite to eat in the city? Big chance it is fatty, salty and unhealthy
'Ticking time bomb': four types of cancer occur more often in young Dutch people
lead: International research by the World Cancer Research Fund shows that various forms of cancer occur more often in people under fifty.

title: Eight 'sugar-free' Starbucks drinks contain sugar, consumers go to court
lead: Consumers started a lawsuit against Starbucks in the United States last week. The coffee chain is accused of adding sugar to drinks that are sold as 'sugar-free'.

title: Whether it all adds up is another matter, but it seems inevitable that a historical figure has an idiosyncratic character
'It seems as if the government is giving up the fight for accessibility'
lead: Only 5 percent of the websites and apps of the Dutch government meet the accessibility requirements. Meanwhile, accessibility expert Jules Ernst sees some government websites even getting worse. 'A regulator was already promised in 2024, but nothing is happening.'

title: Asylum minister Van den Brink wants to punish asylum seeker who frustrates deportation

Shortly before time, Merino plucked a pass out of the air, turned on his axis and shot the ball with that same left foot into the near corner
Gordon no longer suffers from type 2 diabetes: can that happen by changing your lifestyle?
lead: "Look, there are my insulin syringes. Bye, no longer needed," Gordon points out in a video on social media. Through his new lifestyle, the singer says he no longer suffers from diabetes. But fully recovering from that disease is not possible. Here is how it works.

title: Bertram wants to combine public transport and other types of transport in the region
lead: Public transport and, among other things, pupil transport must be combined in regions where accessibility is declining. State Secretary <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Annet Bertram</entity> (Infrastructure, CDA) wants in that way to move from public transport to 'public mobility' that can be booked all day for everyone, she writes in a letter to the House.

title: An absurd project with a cubic kilometre of polar ice was able to capture elusive particles
lead: The Belgian Francis Halzen receives the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on IceCube, a telescope on Antarctica to detect neutrinos. "No respectable, conservative physicist joined me"

title: Quackery award goes to football club Ajax
lead: Football club Ajax receives the Meester Kackadorisprijs 2026, the Vereniging tegen de Kwakzalverij (VtdK) announced on Friday. The association awards the prize annually to a person or organisation that "promotes quackery, without practising it itself". Ajax receives the prize because of the football club's sponsorship agreement with supplement company Vitakruid.
